items.title: Supporting Cast Pair for 'Shin Oishinbo' Announced
items.summary: The official website for the television anime adaptation of Tetsu Kariya's Oishinbo manga, titled Shin Oishinbo, announced a supporting pair of cast on Thursday. The anime is scheduled to premiere in 2027. Voice actors Kenji Yamauchi (Toujima Tanzaburou wa Kamen Rider ni Naritai) and Ken Uo (Nazotoki wa Dinner no Ato de) are joining the anime as Mantarou Kyougoku and Toujin Touyama, respectively. Kenichi Nishida (Sayounara Ryuusei, Konnichiwa Jinsei) is directing the anime at SynergySP and Vega Entertainment. Takahiro Nagano (Tensei shitara Ken deshita) is handling the series composition, while Nozomi Kawashige (Deatte 5-byou de Battle) is designing the characters. Kariya began writing Oishinbo in Shogakukan's Big Comic Spirits magazine in 1983, featuring art by Akira Hanasaki. Shogakukan published the 111th and latest volume in December 2014. The manga has been on hiatus since May 2014. VIZ Media licensed the manga in English and published seven themed compilation volumes under its VIZ Signature imprint from January 2009 to January 2010. Shin-Ei Animation produced a television anime based on the manga that ran for 136 episodes from October 1988 to March 1992. Source: Official Site

items.title: 'Nabe ni Tama wo Ukenagara' Reveals Main Cast, Staff, Teaser Promo, Winter 2027 Premiere
items.summary: Production company Asmik Ace opened an official website for a television anime adaptation of Juntarou Aoki and Shin Moriyama's Nabe ni Tama wo Ukenagara (Getting Shots on Frying Pan) manga on Thursday, revealing the main cast, staff, and a teaser promotional video. Produced by J.C.Staff, the anime is scheduled to premiere on Nippon TV, Yomiuri TV, BS Nippon TV, and AT-X in January 2027. Voice actors Shuu Uchida (Yarinaoshi Reijou wa Ryuutei Heika wo Kouryakuchuu) and Masaaki Mizunaka (Nyaight of the Living Cat) are voicing the beautiful girl and male versions of Juntarou Aoki, respectively. Staff Director: Masahiro Hiraoka (Kabushikigaisha Magi-Lumière) Series Composition, Script: Susumu Yamakawa (Maiko-san Chi no Makanai-san) Character Design, Chief Animation Director: Natsuki Ooyama (Danjo no Yuujou wa Seiritsu suru? (Iya, Shinai!!)) Music: Yoshihide Ootomo (Inu-Ou) Sound Director: Yoshikazu Iwanami (Kujima Utaeba Ie Hororo) Aoki began serializing the slice of life manga, with illustrations by Moriyama, on Comic Newtype website in May 2021. Kadokawa published the fifth volume in October 2024. A spin-off series titled Nabe ni Tama wo Ukenagara Transit featuring Hirota Takahara, began serializing on March 20. Teaser PV Official site: https://nabetama.asmik-ace.co.jp/ Source: Comic Natalie

items.title: LiSA en concert au Zénith de Paris
items.summary: Concerts et festivals / Musique 0 LiSA en concert au Zénith de Paris par Tatiana Chedebois · Publié 12 novembre 2026 · Mis à jour 11 novembre 2026 LiSA était en concert au Zénith de Paris le 20 septembre 2026. Le concert était complet en quelques minutes lors de la mise en vente. 6000 fans ont répondu présents pour sa première tournée mondiale. Cette escale en France a été un succès massif dans le paysage français de J-music un peu morose en 2026. LiSA est une chanteuse d’anisong que vous avez sans aucun doute déjà entendue au moins une fois. Avec notamment ses titres iconiques interprétés pour Demon slayer . Qui est LiSA ? LiSA , de son vrai nom Risa Oribe , est une chanteuse japonaise née le 24 juin dans la préfecture de Gifu, au Japon. Elle commence à se faire connaître en 2010 grâce à l’anime Angel Beats!, dans lequel elle prête sa voix chantée au personnage de Yui , membre du groupe fictif Girls Dead Monster. En 2011, elle lance sa carrière solo avec le mini-album Letters to U . Elle gagne ensuite en popularité en interprétant des chansons pour des animes célèbres, notamment Fate/Zero avec oath sign et Sword Art Online avec crossing field . Grâce à sa voix puissante, son énergie et son style mêlant rock et pop japonaise, elle devient rapidement une artiste incontournable dans le milieu de l’ anisong. La carrière de LiSA connaît un immense succès en 2019 avec Gurenge , le générique d’ouverture de l’anime Demon Slayer , qui va conquérir un large public tant au Japon qu’à l’international. items.title: Interview: Blue Box Season 2 Director Daisuke Sako on Taiki & Chinatsu Focus and Adaptation Process
items.summary: Interview Interview: Blue Box Season 2 Director Daisuke Sako on Taiki & Chinatsu Focus and Adaptation Process Written by Jorge Manuel Sanchez Moreno Cardenas November 12, 2026 As one of the most outstanding romance stories in recent years, Blue Box highlights the inner worlds and unique sensibilities of its whole cast of characters. The story combines the romantic pursuits of the protagonists, Taiki and Chinatsu, with the passion of spokon , and the adventure of growing up from adolescence. While the Blue Box manga officially ended on July 13 , we can still follow our favorite characters in the anime adaptation currently airing. Blue Box Season 2 explores new sides of the cast and introduces the long awaited Yumeka Goto, a person from Chinatsu’s past. That’s why we were excited to interview Season 2 director Daisuke Sako about Yumeka, the themes explored during the season, and his takes on the story’s message. © Kouji Miura/SHUEISHA, Blue Box Film Partners. Q: Were there any specific themes or core elements you particularly focused on for Season 2? A: This time, we wanted to recreate real, named places as faithfully as possible. The idea that “these characters live in this particular kind of town in Japan” was something we valued in the anime as well. We didn’t only feature the obvious, well-known spots.
